analysis.title: US Daily: October Payrolls Preview
key_insights: GS estimates October nonfarm payrolls rose 75k, above consensus of +65k and the three-month average of +51k, reflecting low layoffs and a solid signal from big data indicators.
GS estimates private payrolls rose 70k in October versus consensus of +64k.
GS forecasts average hourly earnings up 0.3% month-over-month, in line with consensus, reflecting neutral calendar effects.

GS estimates the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.2% on a rounded basis, in line with consensus, but sees risks skewed toward a lower reading as the rate may converge to the lower level implied by continuing claims.

Layoffs are low. Initial jobless claims averaged 198k in the October payroll month versus 204k in September, the JOLTS layoff rate fell 0.1pp to 1.0% in September, and Challenger announced layoffs rose 1k to 53k (SA by GS).
Alternative employment data tracked by GS averaged roughly +70k in October, slightly above consensus.

Residual seasonality favors a rebound. When Labor Day falls late in September (the 7th this year), September payrolls tend to underperform and October accelerates by roughly 50k on average. September payrolls rose 29k.

Employer surveys point weaker. The employment components of GS's manufacturing tracker (-0.5pt to 52.6) and services tracker (-0.8pt to 50.8) declined in October, but GS says survey signals have been less useful and at times misleading since the pandemic, so they carry limited weight in the forecast.

Job availability is mixed. GS estimates job openings edged slightly higher in September, Indeed and LinkUp measures were roughly stable in October, and the Conference Board labor differential rose 2.4pt to +5.3.
GS's wage tracker rose 3.0% quarter-over-quarter annualized and 3.3% year-over-year in Q3.

GS's slack tracker, scaled to unemployment-rate-equivalent units, has declined in recent months but stands at 4.6%, suggesting the labor market is somewhat softer than the 4.2% unemployment rate implies.
